Overall system engineering and technology development activities for the module are progressing across ISRO Centres and Units. The Minister further informed that the Union Cabinet approved a budgetary allocation of ₹20,193 crore in September 2024 for the execution of eight missions under India's Human Spaceflight Programme. He also highlighted ISRO's collaborations with leading international space agencies, including the European Space Agency (ESA) for network operations support, the Australian Space Agency (ASA) for crew and crew module recovery, France's CNES for specialised training of flight surgeons and ground support teams, and Russia's Roscosmos for astronaut training and procurement of critical human spaceflight systems. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the progress achieved under the Gaganyaan Mission, together with the roadmap for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station, reflects the Government's sustained commitment to strengthening India's indigenous human spaceflight capabilities and building the technological foundations for the country's future space exploration programme. *** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295557)

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INDIA’S POSITION IN GLOBAL LAUNCH MARKET
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INDIA’S POSITION IN GLOBAL LAUNCH MARKET प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 2:48PM by PIB Delhi The LVM3-M6 mission successfully deployed the US-based AST Space Mobile's BlueBird Block-2 communication satellite, into Low Earth Orbit (LEO) of 520km circular, which is the heaviest payload (6100kg) to be launched by LVM3 from Indian soil. This launch has demonstrated India's technological prowess, which has significantly enhanced commercial confidence in LVM3 launch vehicle, thereby becoming one of the preferred launch vehicles in the international commercial launch services market. Government is pursuing international space cooperation for providing strategic and technological gains to Indian space program. Meeting targets of Space Vision 2047 including human spaceflight, space station and space exploration missions is the core component of such efforts. Enhancing launch capability, widening ground station network, expanding space infrastructure and application base, promoting participation of Indian space industries in international exhibitions & business forums, B2B engagements and integrating Indian industries into global supply chains also forms part of international cooperation strategy. Government has also established dialogue mechanisms and joint innovation roadmaps with partner countries to gain from their technological expertise and strategic benefits. In order to expand the country's role as a reliable provider of space services, the Government is enabling the private sector through IN-SPACe to develop indigenous capabilities across the space sector, including the launch vehicle segment. Some of the key initiatives undertaken are: Development of the second spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam, Tamil Nadu, to augment India's launch infrastructure and facilitate increased participation of the private sector in launch vehicle operations. Establishment of a stringent review and authorization mechanism to enhance the safety, reliability, and quality of launch systems. Development of Indian space standards in collaboration with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) to promote standardization and quality assurance across the space sector. Facilitating and enabling readiness of Skyroot, Agnikul, HAL for getting their respective launch vehicles ready. The following initiatives/schemes have been announced by IN-SPACe in order to enable, promote participation of private enterprises in space activities: Released the India Space Policy 2023, where the roles and responsibilities of all the contributors of Indian Space Eco systems defined. Implementation of a discounted pricing policy to enable Non-Government Entities (NGEs) to access ISRO facilities. Establishment of a ₹1,000 Cr. Venture Capital (VC) Fund to support space start-ups. title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ISRO-SUPPORTED SPACE TECHNOLOGY APPLICATIONS IN JAMMU & KASHMIR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ISRO-SUPPORTED SPACE TECHNOLOGY APPLICATIONS IN JAMMU & KASHMIR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 2:45PM by PIB Delhi ISRO/DoS has implemented several satellite-based applications and space technology programmes in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir during the last five years. Among the operational communication satellites, 12 satellites have the coverage over the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. This capacity is offered to various service providers to meet and enhance the telecommunication and broadband connectivity. ISRO/DoS has undertaken the following projects for disaster management, agriculture, water resources, urban planning and environmental monitoring in Jammu & Kashmir: Satellite Integrated Landslide Assessment and Alert System (SILAAS) project (under ISRO-DMSP): to map landslides using satellite; and for generation of village-wise landslide alerts. Landslide inventory mapping for the 2023 monsoon season, covering all districts of Jammu & Kashmir Under the National Hydrology Project, an inventory of glacial lakes has been carried out for Jammu & Kashmir, and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF) hazard and risk maps have been generated for Mundiksar lake in the Indus River basin. Monitoring of the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) watersheds using geospatial technologies covering the districts of Anantnag, Bandipora, Baramulla, Budgam, Doda, Ganderbal, Jammu, Kathua, Kishtwar, Kulgam, Kupwara, Poonch, Pulwama, Rajouri, Ramban, Reasi, Samba, Shopian, Srinagar & Udhampur Monitoring of the Watershed Development Component- Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY) 2.0 projects, covering the districts of Anantnag, Bandipora, Baramulla, Budgam, Doda, Ganderbal, Jammu, Kathua, Kishtwar, Kulgam, Kupwara, Poonch, Pulwama, Rajouri, Ramban, Reasi, Samba, Shopian, Srinagar & Udhampur. Under the Urban Waterbody Information System (UWaIS) project (AMRUT 2.0), waterbodies have been mapped for Anantnag, Jammu and Srinagar. Geo-MGNREGA Project (Phase II) - covering the districts of Anantnag, Bandipora, Baramulla, Budgam, Doda, Ganderbal, Jammu, Kathua, Kishtwar, Kulgam, Kupwara, Poonch, Pulwama, Rajouri, Ramban, Reasi, Samba, Shopian, Srinagar & Udhampur for planning and monitoring the MGNREGA activities. National Wetland Inventory and Assessment (NWIA) project (2021-22), with the University of Jammu: wetland inventory and district-wise analysis of wetlands for Jammu & Kashmir. Desertification and Land Degradation: Monitoring, Vulnerability Assessment and Combating Plan project (2018-19), with the University of Kashmir, Srinagar: status mapping and vulnerability assessment for Kathua, Budgam and Udhampur districts, along with preparation of an action plan for combating land degradation for a micro-watershed in the region. Long Term Ecological Research Stations (LTERS) project (2021-2025): Climate and Ecosystem Response Studies, covering the North-West Himalaya, including Jammu & Kashmir. Space Based Information Support for Decentralised Planning - Update (SISDP-U) Project for all districts of Jammu and Kashmir, generating thematic information on land use, settlements, infrastructure and drainage from high-resolution satellite data. Satellite-based annual assessment of Land Use/Land Cover at 1:2,50,000 scale has been carried out for 2021-22 to 2024-25, along with a five-yearly assessment at 1:50,000 scale for 2020-21. The year-wise details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised, along with beneficiary departments/implementing agencies, are as under: Sl. ISRO periodically conducts national and regional workshops and training programmes for State and Central disaster management organisations, including regional training on the National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM), in which participants from Jammu & Kashmir have taken part. ISRO has established Satish Dhawan Centre for Space Science (SDCSS) at Central University of Jammu, Jammu where faculty/research students are provided access to ISRO facilities to support learning and enhance understanding on space technology. Tele-education is facilitated through satellites under PM e-Vidya programme. Telemedicine nodes are installed in the Jammu and Kashmir regions under telemedicine programme. In 2024, a High Throughput Satellite (HTS) namely GSAT-N2 is added to enhance the broadband connectivity including Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Atomic Energy, Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. **** NKR/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295423) आगंतुक पटल  : 225 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ISRO-SUPPORTED SPACE TECHNOLOGY APPLICATIONS IN JAMMU & KASHMIR प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Coal Supply Position for Power Sector Remains Adequate; Production and Despatch Register Strong Growth in July 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal Coal Supply Position for Power Sector Remains Adequate; Production and Despatch Register Strong Growth in July 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi The country's coal supply position for the power sector continues to remain adequate, backed by robust growth in production, despatch and receipts during July 2026. The overall coal production during July 2026 stood at 69.75 Million Tonnes (MT), as against 64.88 MT during the corresponding period last year, registering a growth of 7.51%. Overall coal despatch during the month stood even higher, at 86.85 MT compared to 73.58 MT in the same period last year, marking a robust growth of 18.03%. The coal receipt at thermal power plants during July 2026 stood at 68.83 MT, as against 60.69 MT in July 2025, registering a growth of 13.41%. This sustained and healthy growth in supplies to the power sector underscores the Ministry's continued focus on ensuring uninterrupted coal availability to meet the nation's energy requirements, with the continued support of Indian Railways. As on 04.08.2026, the coal stock at thermal power plants stood at 34.55 MT. In addition, about 113 MT of coal is available at pitheads and in transit, taking the total available stock to approximately 148 MT. This is adequate to meet about 62 days of the power sector's coal consumption requirement, providing a comfortable buffer. The Ministry of Coal remains fully committed to ensuring uninterrupted and adequate coal supply to all consumers, particularly the power sector, to support the nation's growing energy needs. This sustained performance reflects the Ministry's unwavering commitment to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat, ensuring energy security and self-reliance for the country. The Ministry continues to closely monitor the coal supply chain, to ensure that the power sector's requirements are met without disruption. *** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295461) आगंतुक पटल  : 240 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Coal Coal Supply Position for Power Sector Remains Adequate; Production and Despatch Register Strong Growth in July 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

As on 04.08.2026, the coal stock at thermal power plants stood at 34.55 MT. In addition, about 113 MT of coal is available at pitheads and in transit, taking the total available stock to approximately 148 MT. This is adequate to meet about 62 days of the power sector's coal consumption requirement, providing a comfortable buffer. The Ministry of Coal remains fully committed to ensuring uninterrupted and adequate coal supply to all consumers, particularly the power sector, to support the nation's growing energy needs. This sustained performance reflects the Ministry's unwavering commitment to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat, ensuring energy security and self-reliance for the country. The Ministry continues to closely monitor the coal supply chain, to ensure that the power sector's requirements are met without disruption. *** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295461)

title: Bhubaneswari OCP: Where Innovation Powers Production and Sustainability Shapes Growth
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal Bhubaneswari OCP: Where Innovation Powers Production and Sustainability Shapes Growth प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 2:34PM by PIB Delhi In India's journey towards becoming a global economic powerhouse, Bhubaneswari Opencast Project (OCP) of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) stands as a Prime Example of the harmonious integration of productivity, technology and sustainability. Located in the coal-rich Talcher Coalfield of Odisha, Bhubaneswari has steadily evolved into one of Coal India Limited's most advanced and productive opencast mines. Operating with a peak rated capacity of 30 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA) , the mine today supplies coal to major thermal power stations that illuminate millions of homes and energize industries across the country. More importantly, Bhubaneswari has demonstrated that large-scale coal production can progress hand in hand with environmental stewardship, technological innovation and community partnership. Performance that Reflects Operational Excellence Bhubaneswari's operational achievements reflect meticulous planning and consistent execution. During FY 2025–26 , the mine produced 26.477 million tonnes of coal against an Annual Action Plan target of 25 million tonnes , achieving an impressive 105.98% of its target. Since its inception, the project has produced an extraordinary 370.4 million tonnes of coal , underscoring its enduring contribution to India's energy sector. The momentum has continued into FY 2026–27 , with the production target enhanced to 28 million tonnes . The mine has already recorded 7.62 million tonnes of coal production during the first quarter , reflecting strong operational preparedness and confidence in achieving the enhanced annual target. Technology as a Competitive Advantage At Bhubaneswari, technology is not merely an operational tool—it is a strategic advantage that enhances productivity while reducing environmental impact. The project has distinguished itself by adopting 100% blast-free Surface Miner technology for coal extraction, eliminating the need for drilling and blasting in coal seams. This advanced mining method has improved coal recovery, ensured consistent sizing of coal, minimized dust generation and significantly reduced noise and ground vibrations in surrounding areas. Controlled blasting is restricted only to overburden removal, where advanced electronic delay detonators ensure minimal environmental disturbance. The mine has further strengthened operational efficiency through one of the country's most advanced coal evacuation systems. Covered conveyor networks integrated with 25 MTPA First Mile Connectivity (FMC) SILO infrastructure enable more than 85% of coal dispatch through environmentally friendly rail transport . Bhubaneswari is also home to Coal India Limited's first Automatic Truck Loading System (ATLS) , which has introduced greater speed, transparency and accuracy in truck loading while substantially reducing manual intervention. Creating Growth through Community Partnership The success of a large mining project is measured not only by production but also by its relationship with the communities that surround it. Bhubaneswari has consistently demonstrated that meaningful stakeholder engagement can become a powerful production enabler. Beyond rehabilitation, the project has invested significantly in community infrastructure, including roads, community centres, educational facilities and livelihood support initiatives. Plantation drives, distribution of fruit-bearing and Sal saplings, environmental awareness programmes and other developmental initiatives have strengthened the bond between the project and neighbouring communities, reinforcing the principle that sustainable mining must create shared value. Balancing Productivity with Responsibility Bhubaneswari has established itself as a model for environmentally responsible mining. The project has implemented comprehensive environmental management measures, including continuous air quality monitoring, extensive dust suppression systems, wheel-washing facilities and systematic afforestation programmes supported by a dedicated five-hectare Sal Nursery . These initiatives have earned the project prestigious environmental recognitions, including a Five-Star Rating and the Kalinga Environment Excellence Award , affirming its commitment to ecological stewardship. The project's operational excellence extends equally to safety and financial performance. Maintaining an outstanding zero-fatality record for the last five consecutive years , Bhubaneswari has earned top honours during the Annual Mines Safety Fortnight , reflecting its uncompromising commitment to workplace safety. Financially, the project continues to be one of MCL's strongest contributors, generating a Profit Before Tax of ₹1792.60 crore during FY 2025-26 , further demonstrating that operational excellence and financial sustainability go hand in hand. A Benchmark for the Future Bhubaneswari OCP is far more than a high-capacity coal mine. It is a compelling example of how modern mining can successfully integrate production, technology, environmental responsibility and community development into a single, sustainable growth model. Every tonne of coal produced reflects scientific mine planning, every innovation strengthens operational efficiency, and every community initiative reinforces the project's social commitment. As India's demand for reliable energy continues to rise, Bhubaneswari is well positioned to remain at the forefront of Coal India Limited's growth story. By consistently combining high productivity with technological leadership, responsible environmental practices and inclusive development, the project is setting new benchmarks for the future of sustainable coal mining and making a lasting contribution to the nation's energy security. **** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295419) आगंतुक पटल  : 190 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Coal Bhubaneswari OCP: Where Innovation Powers Production and Sustainability Shapes Growth प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Consultative Committee of Ministry of Coal Discusses Commercial Coal Mining Reforms and Leveraging Private Sector Participation
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal Consultative Committee of Ministry of Coal Discusses Commercial Coal Mining Reforms and Leveraging Private Sector Participation प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 11:16AM by PIB Delhi The Consultative Committee of Members of Parliament attached to the Ministry of Coal met on Wednesday to discuss ‘Commercial Coal Mining Reforms and Leveraging Private Sector Participation’. The meeting was chaired by the Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G Kishan Reddy. It was also attended by the Secretary, Ministry of Coal Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, senior officials of the Ministry and coal PSUs apart from the Members of the Committee. In his opening remarks, Union Minister of Coal and Mines, Shri G Kishan Reddy said that commercial coal mining is one of the shining examples of many reforms introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in last 12 years. Shri Reddy informed the members that 14 rounds of commercial coal mine auctions have already been completed and the 15th round is currently under process. The Minister also said that commercial coal mining have made the coal sector more competitive and efficient. Shri Reddy said that transparent auction process has transformed India’s Coal Sector by promoting competition and investment. Referring to the auction process, Shri Reddy said that the Ministry of Coal is actively engaging with industry bodies and private companies by organizing roadshows and stakeholder consultations, to ensure greater awareness and wider participation. While welcoming the members, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Shri Vikram Dev Dutt said the captive and commercial mines have played an important role in achieving 1 Billion Tonne coal production in last two financial years. Shri Dutt highlighted that captive and commercial coal mines have contributed around 20% of the countries coal production in last Financial Year. Secretary also informed that continuous reforms introduced in the coal sector have reduced timelines of operationalization for fully explored blocks from 51 months to 40 months and partially explored blocks from 66 months to 52 months. Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Smt Rupinder Brar gave a presentation on ‘Commercial Coal Mining Reforms and leveraging Private Sector participation’. Members of the Committee appreciated the Ministry's efforts towards reforming the coal sector and offered valuable suggestions on further improving private sector participation and balancing commercial mining growth with environmental and community concerns. Chaired the Consultative Committee Meeting of the Ministries of Coal and Mines with Hon’ble Members of Parliament from across party lines in New Delhi, today. Deliberated on key developments in the sectors and exchanged views on further strengthening the respective sectors.… pic.twitter.com/jKvoRvmEIH — G Kishan Reddy (@kishanreddybjp) August 5, 2026 **** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295327) आगंतुक पटल  : 536 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Bengali , Bengali-TR , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Coal Consultative Committee of Ministry of Coal Discusses Commercial Coal Mining Reforms and Leveraging Private Sector Participation प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: India successfully concludes the Tenth BRICS Industry Ministers' Meeting in Jaipur under its BRICS Chairship 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry India successfully concludes the Tenth BRICS Industry Ministers' Meeting in Jaipur under its BRICS Chairship 2026 BRICS Industry Ministers adopt Joint Declaration to advance industrial growth through enhanced cooperation on MSMEs, Photovoltaics, Startups, and Logistics Framework on Cooperation in SME Working Group promoted to boost the MSME ecosystems Terms of Reference and Action Plan adopted for the BRICS Working Group on the Photovoltaic Industry, establishing a structured framework for cooperation in the sector India proposes BRICS Incubator Network and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund to support Innovation-led Growth 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting to be Held in Jaipur on August 7 under India's Chairship प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi The Tenth BRICS Industry Ministers' Meeting concluded successfully today in Jaipur, Rajasthan, under India's BRICS Chairship 2026. The meeting brought together Industry Ministers and senior representatives from BRICS member countries to culminate the ministerial engagement under the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution (PartNIR). Held under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,” the meeting provided a platform for member countries to deliberate on strengthening industrial capabilities, harnessing technological transformation, and creating greater opportunities for collaborative action. Addressing the meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry (CIM), welcomed the delegates to Jaipur, describing it as a city that seamlessly blends centuries of craftsmanship with the aspirations of a modern industrial economy. The CIM emphasized that in a rapidly evolving landscape, aspirations must be translated into practical innovation and cooperation. He underscored that BRICS countries must leverage their complementary strengths to build resilient industries and highlighted that PartNIR has evolved into the principal mechanism for this collaboration The Minister of State for Commerce & Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada, reaffirmed India's commitment to fostering stronger industrial partnerships among BRICS Member Countries and highlighted the role of cooperation, innovation and mutual trust in building a resilient and inclusive industrial future. The CIM recalled that the BRICS journey commenced with the inaugural Summit in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. He appreciated Brazil's leadership during its Chairship in 2025 and reaffirmed that Bharat is committed to carrying forward this legacy through an incremental, proactive and pragmatic approach. He noted that India's Chairship seeks to provide continuity while fostering greater confidence among businesses, investors and innovators, and advancing practical cooperation that delivers tangible outcomes for all BRICS members. The CIM apprised the gathering of the significant progress achieved under India's BRICS Chairship through PartNIR. He also highlighted the outcomes of the extensive deliberations undertaken by the Advisory Group and the thematic Working Groups across the four priority areas identified by India, aimed at establishing enduring institutional mechanisms to deepen industrial cooperation among BRICS member countries. These included the finalisation of the Framework for Cooperation in the SME Working Group, the adoption of Terms of Reference and Action Plan for Working Group on Photovoltaic Industry, finalisation of the Action Plan on innovation-led growth by Startups. Further, the importance of resilient industry related transport and logistics systems, including GIS-based Infrastructure Planning and City Logistics Planning were highlighted. A major outcome of the meeting was the adoption of the Joint Declaration of the Tenth BRICS Industry Ministers’ Meeting. The Declaration reflects the collective commitment of member countries to move beyond dialogue toward the implementation of practical instruments of cooperation that strengthen industries and improve lives. During the Meeting, Industry Ministers and Heads of Delegation from BRICS Member Countries shared their national perspectives, highlighting key policy initiatives, priorities, and achievements in promoting industrial development. The statements underscored a shared commitment to strengthening industrial capabilities, accelerating digital and technological transformation, fostering resilient and inclusive industrial ecosystems, and enhancing cooperation to address common development challenges. Member countries reaffirmed the importance of the PartNIR as a key platform for advancing practical collaboration, knowledge sharing, capacity building, and industrial innovation among BRICS members. Delegations also welcomed the progress made under India's 2026 Chairship, noting that the initiatives undertaken under PartNIR would contribute to strengthening institutional cooperation, fostering innovation and capacity building, and supporting the development of resilient, competitive, and future-ready industries across BRICS. India, under its BRICS Chairship, is also hosting the 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting (TMM) in Jaipur, Rajasthan, on 7 August 2026, following the Third Meeting of the BRICS Contact Group on Economic and Trade Issues (CGETI) which was held on 3rd and 4th August 2026 in New Delhi. The Ministerial Meeting will be chaired by Shri Piyush Goyal, Union Minister of Commerce & Industry and attended by Shri Jitin Prasada, Union Minister of State for Commerce & Industry and Shri Rajesh Agrawal, Commerce Secretary. The Meeting will bring together Trade Ministers and senior officials from BRICS Member Countries to deliberate on key issues relating to international trade and economic cooperation. Under the overarching theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," deliberations have focused on advancing economic cooperation among BRICS Member Countries. Discussions under the Third Contact Group on Economic and Trade Issues (CGETI) have centered on strengthening the multilateral trading system, enhancing the participation of MSMEs in international trade, fostering resilient and diversified global value chains, and facilitating seamless cross-border digitally delivered services. During the Trade Ministerial deliberations, the visiting Ministers and their delegations will participate in a cultural excursion to City Palace and Hawa Mahal showcasing India's rich heritage and traditions. The technical sessions will provide an opportunity for Ministers to exchange views on strengthening trade and economic cooperation among BRICS Member Countries. The BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting marks a significant milestone under India's BRICS Chairship and reaffirms India's commitment to promoting an open, inclusive, transparent, equitable and rules-based multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core. The deliberations are expected to contribute to India's vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 by fostering resilient supply chains, innovation-driven growth, stronger MSME participation in international trade, and deeper economic cooperation among emerging economies. *** Abhishek Dayal/Abhijith Narayanan/Shabbir Azad (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295733) आगंतुक पटल  : 64 Ministry of Commerce & Industry India successfully concludes the Tenth BRICS Industry Ministers' Meeting in Jaipur under its BRICS Chairship 2026 BRICS Industry Ministers adopt Joint Declaration to advance industrial growth through enhanced cooperation on MSMEs, Photovoltaics, Startups, and Logistics Framework on Cooperation in SME Working Group promoted to boost the MSME ecosystems Terms of Reference and Action Plan adopted for the BRICS Working Group on the Photovoltaic Industry, establishing a structured framework for cooperation in the sector India proposes BRICS Incubator Network and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund to support Innovation-led Growth 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting to be Held in Jaipur on August 7 under India's Chairship प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi Recent claims in the media suggesting that India is importing and intends to import large quantities of ethanol from the United States (U.S.) for fuel blending are baseless and factually incorrect. As per the domestic policy framework, ethanol used for fuel blending under the Ethanol Blended with Petrol Programme is sourced entirely from domestic producers. There is no import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S. Further, no concessions or commitments relating to the import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S. have been made in the India-U.S. Trade discussions. Accordingly, any suggestion of a policy change to permit large-scale imports of fuel ethanol from the U.S. is misleading. India’s fuel blending programme and ethanol procurement continues to be governed solely by India’s domestic policy requirements. *** Abhishek Dayal/ Ishita Biswas (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295653) आगंतुक पटल  : 385 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati , Telugu , Malayalam Ministry of Commerce & Industry No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Announces Tentative Schedule for Patent and Trade Marks Agent Examinations 2027 at 15 Centres Across India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Announces Tentative Schedule for Patent and Trade Marks Agent Examinations 2027 at 15 Centres Across India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (O/o CGPDTM) has announced that the Trade Marks Agent Examination (TAE) 2027 is likely to be held on 9 January 2027 (Saturday), while the Patent Agent Examination (PAE) 2027 is likely to be conducted on 10 January 2027 (Sunday). The examinations are proposed to be held at 15 centres across the country, namely Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Indore, Jodhpur, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Pune and Thiruvananthapuram. The Patent Agent Examination is conducted by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks in accordance with Rule 110 of the Patents Rules, 2003 (as amended) read with Section 126 of the Patents Act, 1970 (as amended). The Trade Marks Agent Examination is conducted in accordance with Rule 144 of the Trade Marks Rules, 2017. Both the Patent Agent Examination and the Trade Marks Agent Examination comprise three stages: Paper I consisting of objective-type multiple choice questions carrying 100 marks, Paper II comprising a subjective/descriptive paper carrying 100 marks, and a Viva Voce carrying 50 marks to assess the candidate's ability and suitability to practise before the Intellectual Property Office. Candidates are required to secure a minimum of 50 marks each in Paper I and Paper II. title: SAFEGUARDING INDIA'S INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture SAFEGUARDING INDIA'S INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 2:54PM by PIB Delhi The 20th Session of the Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage (20.COM), convened under the UNESCO 2003 Convention, was hosted by the Government of India at the Red Fort (Lal Qila), New Delhi, from 8 to 13 December 2025. The Session marked a historic milestone as it was the first time that India hosted the Intergovernmental Committee under the UNESCO 2003 Convention. It also coincided with the twentieth anniversary of India's ratification of the Convention, reaffirming India's longstanding commitment to safeguarding living heritage and strengthening international cultural cooperation. The Session witnessed the participation of approximately 1,200 delegates from around 130 countries, including representatives of States Parties, members of the Intergovernmental Committee, UNESCO officials, accredited non-governmental organisations, cultural institutions, experts and community practitioners. It served as an important global platform for policy dialogue, exchange of best practices and international cooperation in the safeguarding of intangible cultural heritage. The principal objectives of hosting the Session were to enhance the global visibility of India's rich and diverse living heritage; showcase its community-based safeguarding practices; contribute to international discussions on intangible cultural heritage and sustainable development; and strengthen India's leadership in international cultural cooperation under the UNESCO 2003 Convention. A landmark outcome of the Session was the inscription of Deepavali on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. With this inscription, Deepavali became the 16th intangible cultural heritage element from India to be inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage Lists. The inscription accorded international recognition to one of India's most significant festivals, reflecting the universal values of harmony, cultural continuity, social cohesion and shared traditions, while reaffirming India's sustained commitment to safeguarding, promoting and transmitting its rich living heritage in accordance with the principles of the UNESCO 2003 Convention. With the inscription of Deepavali, in December 2025 a total of 16 intangible cultural heritage elements from India have been inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The detailed procedure/mechanism for preparing nomination dossiers are laid down in the Operational Directives of UNESCO 2003 Convention and is available on https://ich.unesco.org/en/directives . Government took a decision to nominate Chhath Mahaparva as Multinational Nomination. Accordingly, amongst other countries Mauritius was also contacted which showed keen interest in joining this Multinational nomination. Thereafter dossier was prepared which included ICH 01 form, movie, consent letters etc. The completed dossier was sent to UNESCO. Sangeet Natak Akademi (SNA) which is Nodal Agency for UNESCO nomination for Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) elements, maintains National Inventory on ICH wherein 54 elements are listed and ready for the nomination.  However, UNESCO Directive permits only one nomination in two years cycle. This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today *** M Annadurai (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295431) आगंतुक पटल  : 266 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Culture SAFEGUARDING INDIA'S INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:

                06 AUG 2026 2:51PM by PIB Delhi There are 3688 centrally protected monuments/sites under the jurisdiction of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in the country. ASI undertakes conservation of these Monuments and sites as per the National Conservation Policy. The periodical condition assessments and day to day maintenance of these monuments and sites are carried out on regular basis as per the requirement and availability of resources. The details of funds allocated and utilized for conservation and preservation of these monuments during the last five years, State-wise are given at Annexure-I. The ASI undertakes conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments, including lesser-known monuments. Visitor amenities such as pathways, signage, drinking water, toilets, benches, cultural notice board and site museums are developed, wherever feasible. ASI promotes heritage awareness through digital initiatives, cultural programmes, exhibitions, outreach programmes and dissemination of information on the occasion of World Heritage Day, World Heritage Week, Museum Day and other such type of occasions/events. ASI also conducts Seminars and workshops for students and scholars to impart a deeper knowledge on our vast cultural heritage. Further, Ministry of Tourism promotes tourism destination and products of the country, in a holistic manner, including cultural and heritage tourism and lesser-known destinations. The promotions are undertaken through several initiatives such as organizing tourism promotional events, held in association with tourism stakeholders, digital promotion through social media handles in collaboration with social media influencers and showcasing the tourism destinations and products through the Incredible India Digital portal. Additionally, several stakeholder engagements are regionally organized by the India Tourism offices, to promote and raise awareness about these destinations, under the Dekho Apna Desh initiative. There are 3688 monuments/sites under the care and maintenance of ASI, including lesser-known monuments. These sites are regularly inspected by the technical staff of ASI and the conservation, maintenance and development works are planned and executed based on the condition, priority and requirement of the monuments subject to the availability of resources. title: NATIONAL PROGRAMME ON LIBRARIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture NATIONAL PROGRAMME ON LIBRARIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 2:50PM by PIB Delhi Library is a state subject as per the Seventh schedule of Constitution of India, and public libraries function under the administrative control of the respective State/Union Territory Authorities. However, Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation (RRRLF), an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, has been implementing schemes for the promotion and development of public libraries across the country. RRRLF supports their strengthening by providing financial assistance for infrastructure development, library services, reading resources and capacity building. RRRLF extends financial assistance for development of public libraries under its various Matching and Non-matching schemes for construction/renovation of library buildings, procurement of books and reading materials, purchase of furniture and equipment, and improvement of library infrastructure. Assistance is also provided for strengthening ICT-enabled library services, and for the digitisation of copyright-free manuscripts, rare documents and other heritage materials, wherever admissible under the scheme guidelines. Through these interventions, public libraries are encouraged to function as inclusive centres for reading, cultural engagement, lifelong learning and community participation. RRRLF also promotes the sharing and dissemination of best practices through interactions with State Library Authorities, workshops, seminars, conferences and meetings of State Library Planning Committees with a view to improving the quality of library services across the country. The Ministry of Culture also implements the National Mission on Libraries (NML) Scheme, under which financial assistance is provided through the Setting up of NML Model Library component to one State Central Library and one District Library in each State /UT, as recommended by the concerned State Authorities, along with six libraries identified by the Ministry of Culture. Ministry of Culture has implemented a National Virtual Library of India (NVLI) through the Indian Culture Portal, www.indianculture.gov.in under NML Scheme. The objective of NVLI is to provide a platform for the digital preservation of diverse cultural artefacts and to create awareness and a sense of collective ownership among citizens about their shared heritage. The National Archives of India (NAI) under Ministry of Culture has digitized approximately 19.7 crore pages and the digital repository currently hosts around 74.7 lakh reference media files accessible through the Abhilekh Patal portal ( https://www.abhilekh-patal.in ). This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today *** M Annadurai (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295429) आगंतुक पटल  : 193 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Culture NATIONAL PROGRAMME ON LIBRARIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Status of the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture Status of the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 2:49PM by PIB Delhi The National Council of Science Museums (NCSM), an autonomous body under Ministry of Culture, serves as the nodal agency for implementation of Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS). This scheme is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, aimed at fostering scientific temper and awareness across the country for the public in general and students in particularalso to portray the growth of science and technology and their application in industry and human welfare and to create, inculcate and sustain a general awareness amongst the people. The scheme supports the establishment of Science Cities, Science Centres, Innovation Hubs, and Digital Planetariums in various regions. The list of such Science Centres, Innovation Hubs and Digital Planetarium established so far, under SPoCS is given in Annexure-A . The actual expenditure incurred by NCSM during last 3(three) financial years under SPoCS is shown in table below: - (Rs. in Lakhs) Sl no. These Science Centres conduct science-based educational activities, exhibitions, demonstrations, innovation programmes and outreach initiatives aimed at promoting scientific temper and encouraging student participation. As on 31.03.2026, a total of 1,68,55,110 visitors including students have visited the Science Centres established under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS). title: Raksha Mantri chairs meeting of Parliamentary Consultative Committee for MoD on Territorial Army
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Raksha Mantri chairs meeting of Parliamentary Consultative Committee for MoD on Territorial Army प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 12:36PM by PIB Delhi Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh chaired a meeting of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Defence in New Delhi on August 6, 2026, with discussions focusing on the ‘Territorial Army’. During the meeting, senior officials presented a detailed briefing on the Territorial Army’s mandate, role and key achievements to the committee members, who offered valuable suggestions to further strengthen the force & enhance its overall effectiveness. In his address, Raksha Mantri described the Territorial Army’s contribution as “significant” in advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s vision of ‘Viksit Bharat’. He emphasised that while the role of the defence forces revolves primarily around security-related aspects, the Territorial Army contributes in other areas such as environmental conservation and social work as well. “The Territorial Army is a living embodiment of the ‘Citizen-Soldier’ concept. While its members engage in civilian pursuits, they simultaneously don the uniform to safeguard the borders and maintain internal security,” he said. Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that the Territorial Army creates surge capacity for the defence forces by building a reserve of trained soldiers who can be deployed immediately whenever the need arises. He added that when the personnel complete their tenure and return to civilian life, they act as a vibrant bridge between society and the military, inspiring the people, especially the youth, to join the defence forces. The Territorial Army stands as a trained, motivated, and potent force, comprising approximately 44,400 personnel and 59 diverse units. Raksha Mantri termed the force as the first responders, who provide immediate relief and support during natural calamities. He acknowledged their role in carrying out relief & rescue work, and providing medical aid to those in need during Kerala floods, Odisha Cyclone & the recent floods in Assam. Commending their contribution in environmental management and climate change mitigation, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the Ecological Task Forces of the Territorial Army have planted approximately 10 crore saplings till date, with the survival rate between 80-85 percent. This green initiative is translating the Prime Minister’s ‘Mission LiFE’ and ‘Panchamrit’ goals into reality on the ground, he said. He also appreciated the efforts of the Territorial Army, deployed in J&K, for taking the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign to greater heights. Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay and other senior officers attended the meeting. **** VK/Sa vvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295354) आगंतुक पटल  : 787 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Bengali , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Defence Raksha Mantri chairs meeting of Parliamentary Consultative Committee for MoD on Territorial Army प्रविष्टि तिथि:

He added that when the personnel complete their tenure and return to civilian life, they act as a vibrant bridge between society and the military, inspiring the people, especially the youth, to join the defence forces. The Territorial Army stands as a trained, motivated, and potent force, comprising approximately 44,400 personnel and 59 diverse units. Raksha Mantri termed the force as the first responders, who provide immediate relief and support during natural calamities. He acknowledged their role in carrying out relief & rescue work, and providing medical aid to those in need during Kerala floods, Odisha Cyclone & the recent floods in Assam. Commending their contribution in environmental management and climate change mitigation, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the Ecological Task Forces of the Territorial Army have planted approximately 10 crore saplings till date, with the survival rate between 80-85 percent. This green initiative is translating the Prime Minister’s ‘Mission LiFE’ and ‘Panchamrit’ goals into reality on the ground, he said. He also appreciated the efforts of the Territorial Army, deployed in J&K, for taking the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign to greater heights. Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay and other senior officers attended the meeting. **** VK/Sa vvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295354)

title: Initiatives for transforming NER
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Development of North-East Region Initiatives for transforming NER प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi The Act East Policy places the North Eastern Region (NER) at the centre of India’s engagement with Southeast Asia. A central focus of the Act East Policy is development of cross-border connectivity infrastructure. The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway and Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project are flagship projects under this framework. The Act East Policy has also strengthened trade linkages between the Northeast and Southeast Asia through development of Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) and Border Haats. The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport project consists of Waterway component and road component. The waterway component has been completed and inaugurated in May, 2023. Road component consists of two lane highway (109 km long) from Paletwa (Myanmar) to Zorinpui, Mizoram. The India-Myanmar-Thailand (IMT) Trilateral Highway has two parts: Road construction in Tamu - Kalewa Highway has been completed and handed over to Govt. of Myanmar in 2009. Construction of Kalewa-Yargi highway-section from km 112 to km 60 is complete and handed over to Government of Myanmar in October 2025. A High-level Task force (HLTF) was constituted, in 2025, on the North East Economic Corridor (NEEC) with a mandate to assess the existing economic, infrastructure and investment ecosystem in NER; to identify critical gaps in physical connectivity, trade facilitation and sectoral investments; and to formulate strategies to attract public and private sector investments in NEEC projects. The report of the HLTF on NEEC was presented in the 73 rd Plenary of North East Council in June, 2026. The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) organized Rising Northeast Investors Summit in May, 2025 to catalyze trade and investment in NER. The focus sectors of the summit identified for attracting investment in NER were Tourism and Hospitality; Agro-Food Processing & allied sectors; Textiles, Handloom and Handicrafts; Healthcare; Education and Skill Development; IT/ITeS; Entertainment & Sports; Infrastructure and Logistics; and Energy. Collectively, the Summit and its pre-event roadshows garnered investment interests of ₹4.48 lakh crore through Memoranda of Understanding (MoU), letters of intent, and qualified leads from private investors, public sector undertakings, and major industrial conglomerates. North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd (NEDFi) plays a pivotal role in strengthening the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector and entrepreneurship developmentin NER by providing financial support for industrial, infrastructure, agri-allied projects, government schemes and institutional support. NEDFi also supports startup ecosystem of NER through North East Venture Fund. title: Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting in Bhubaneswar Tomorrow
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting in Bhubaneswar Tomorrow 3rd BRICS Senior Education Officials Meeting held under India’s BRICS 2026 Chairship Discussions Focus on Building Consensus on Key Elements to be Presented for Consideration and Adoption in the Education Ministers’ Meeting Posted On:
                06 AUG 2026 8:32PM by PIB Delhi Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi will participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ meeting to be held tomorrow in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The Meeting will deliberate on key priorities including Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE), skill development, research and innovation, mutual recognition of qualifications and academic leadership. The Ministry of Education also hosted the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials Meeting (SOM) under India’s BRICS chairship, on August 5, 2026 in Bhubaneswar. The meeting brought senior officials and delegates from BRICS member countries, including Brazil, Russia, China, South Africa, Indonesia, Iran, Ethiopia and United Arab Emirates, to advance cooperation under the BRICS Education Track. The Meeting provided a platform for detailed deliberations on the BRICS Education Ministers’ Declaration. The officials from the BRICS member countries reviewed the proposed text of the Declaration, exchanged views and suggestions, and worked towards building consensus on the key elements to be presented before the Education Ministers for consideration and adoption during the Education Ministers’ Meeting. The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation across key priority areas identified under the BRICS Education Track, including ECCE, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), collaborative research and innovation, mutual recognition of qualifications, academic leadership, and the BRICS’ Guiding Principles on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems. The delegations shared their perspectives and recommendations to further enrich the Declaration and ensure that it reflected the collective aspirations and priorities of BRICS member countries. The deliberations also highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional mechanisms, promoting academic and research collaborations, facilitating exchange of best practices, and enhancing capacity-building initiatives among BRICS countries. The discussions reaffirmed the shared commitment of member countries towards advancing inclusive, resilient and future-ready education systems through greater cooperation, innovation and knowledge exchange. The meeting concluded with the finalization of the proposed outcomes of the BRICS Education Ministers Declaration. The successful conclusion of the Senior Education Officials Meeting marks an important milestone in advancing the priorities of India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, further strengthening cooperation in education among BRICS member countries. *** RRTN (Release ID: 2295761) Visitor Counter : 5 Ministry of Education Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting in Bhubaneswar Tomorrow 3rd BRICS Senior Education Officials Meeting held under India’s BRICS 2026 Chairship Discussions Focus on Building Consensus on Key Elements to be Presented for Consideration and Adoption in the Education Ministers’ Meeting Posted On:

title: IndiaAI Mission Organised AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University to Strengthen India's AI Talent Ecosystem
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT IndiaAI Mission Organised AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University to Strengthen India's AI Talent Ecosystem IndiaAI Mission Deepens Academic Participation through AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, organised the AIKosh University Engagement Programme (UEP) at Chitkara University, Rajpura, on August 6, 2026. The programme aimed to strengthen AI awareness, democratise access to AI resources, and equip students with the knowledge and tools required to participate in India's rapidly growing artificial intelligence ecosystem. Approved by the Government of India in March 2024, the IndiaAI Mission is driving the country's vision of becoming a global leader in artificial intelligence by fostering innovation, enabling responsible AI development, strengthening indigenous AI capabilities, and ensuring that the benefits of AI reach every section of the society. A key pillar of the Mission, AIKosh serves as India's unified data platform, providing access to high-quality datasets, AI models, toolkits, benchmarks and other critical resources that support research and AI application development. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the IndiaAI Mission seeks to introduce students and academic institutions to these national AI assets while encouraging hands-on learning and innovation. As part of the programme, 250+ students from Chitkara University participated in expert sessions, live demonstrations and hands-on activities designed to familiarise them with AIKosh and the broader IndiaAI ecosystem. Participants also explored the AIKosh MCP (Model Context Protocol) and AIKosh SDK (Software Development Kit) which enables users to discover datasets and AI models using natural language, simplifying access to national AI resources and lowering barriers for both developers and non-developers. Speaking on the initiative, Shri Md. Y. Safirulla K IAS, Director, IndiaAI Mission, said: "Guided by the vision of our Honourable Prime Minister to democratize AI, we are committed to ensuring its transformative benefits reach every individual across the nation. This commitment rests upon three foundational pillars—People, Planet, and Progress—a philosophy prominently showcased during the IndiaAI Impact Summit in February 2026. As part of our University Engagement Programme, we will work to showcase the multifaceted elements of India's thriving AI ecosystem across educational institutions nationwide this year." Welcoming the collaboration, Dr. Madhu Chitkara, President and Co-founder, Chitkara University, said: "Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way we learn, innovate, and solve complex challenges. At Chitkara University, we have always believed in preparing our students for the technologies that will shape the future. Our collaboration with the IndiaAI Mission through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme reflects our commitment to nurturing future-ready professionals equipped with the knowledge, skills, and responsible understanding of AI. This initiative will empower our students to engage with cutting-edge AI resources and contribute meaningfully to India's vision of becoming a global AI leader." As part of the next phase of the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, students will be encouraged to contribute datasets through the AIKosh open-source community and the University's institutional profile on AIKosh. They will also be encouraged to enrich existing datasets and develop proof-of-concept AI applications addressing public-good use cases. Outstanding student-led contributions may be considered for future recognition, creating a pathway from AI literacy and dataset exploration to innovation and real-world problem solving. The AIKosh University Engagement Programme is a nationwide initiative designed to deepen AI adoption across higher educational institutions by introducing students, researchers and faculty members to India's national AI infrastructure. Today, AIKosh hosts 14,000+ Datasets, 300+ AI models and 30+ Toolkits, enabling researchers, startups, developers and students to build AI solutions using trusted national resources. The programme at Chitkara University marks another step towards building a vibrant AI-ready talent pool and advancing the IndiaAI Mission's vision of creating an inclusive, responsible and innovation-driven AI ecosystem for the nation. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the Mission will continue to engage academic institutions across the country, fostering campus-level AI communities that contribute to datasets, models, applications, research and responsible AI adoption. **** Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295677) आगंतुक पटल  : 100 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Punjabi Ministry of Electronics & IT IndiaAI Mission Organised AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University to Strengthen India's AI Talent Ecosystem IndiaAI Mission Deepens Academic Participation through AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Government Expands Digital Infrastructure and Citizen-Centric Services to Bridge the Digital Divide
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT Government Expands Digital Infrastructure and Citizen-Centric Services to Bridge the Digital Divide 2.21 Lakh Gram Panchayats Made Service Ready Under BharatNet; 5.01 Lakh Common Service Centres Deliver Digital Services Nationwide प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 AUG 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister's vision to democratise technology and empower citizens, the Government of India had launched the Digital India programme in July, 2015. At its core, the programme promotes three interconnected goals: strengthening digital infrastructure, delivering government services digitally, and empowering citizens through digital literacy and employment. The Government is implementing the Digital India Programme through a whole-of-government approach to provide efficient, transparent and accessible digital services across the country. The Programme focuses on expanding digital infrastructure, broadband connectivity, digital inclusion and citizen-centric e-Governance services for all eligible citizens, including those in rural and remote areas. Details of some of the key initiatives are as follows: Internet connectivity: Digital India has contributed to the rapid expansion of internet access, through initiatives such as BharatNet, which aims to provide high-speed internet to rural and remote areas. As a result, there has been a substantial increase in internet accessibility and usage across the country, and internet penetration in India has grown in the last decade. ● Telecom, Internet & Broadband Penetration: Total telephone connections in India grew from 93.3 crores in March 2014 to 133+ crores in March, 2026. In Tamil Nadu, the total number of telephone subscribers has crossed 8.41 crore. ●   Internet subscribers jumped from 25.15 crore in March 2014 to 109.27 crore in March, 2026. In Tamil Nadu, the total number of internet subscribers has crossed 6.90 crore. ● BharatNet - Linking Villages to the Internet: As of June 2026, about 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) have been made service ready under BharatNet project in the country. There are 9,280 operational GPs in Tamil Nadu, including 210 GPs in Dharampuri. ●  Under the Government-funded 4G Saturation Project and other mobile connectivity projects, till June 2026, 257 mobile towers have been commissioned in Tamil Nadu. ●  As on 30.06.2026, 24,784 Towers are commissioned across the country under Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) funded mobile scheme. The status in the state of Tamil Nadu including Dharmapuri District of Tamil Nadu is as under: Towers planned Villages planned Towers on Air Villages covered Tamil Nadu 356 445 257 308 Dharmapuri District 14 22 11 19 ●  As on 30.06.2026, a total of Rs. 1886 crores have been disbursed under various ongoing projects of Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) in Tamil Nadu. Services delivery through Digital Public Infrastructure: Affordable data, assisted digital access points, and interoperable public platforms are enabling citizens to access welfare schemes, make digital payments, pursue online education, and participate in governance. Data costs have plummeted from Rs. 269 per GB in 2014 to roughly Rs. 8-10 per Giga Byte in 2025-26, making India one of the world's cheapest data markets. ● Aadhaar: Aadhaar created a trusted biometric identity platform for secure and instant digital authentication. Over 1.44+ billion Aadhaar numbers have been generated. In Tamil Nadu, over 8.18 crore Aadhaar have been generated. ● Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT): Through Aadhaar-linked DBT, cash benefits from various welfare schemes (318 Schemes of 56 Ministries) are directly transferred into beneficiaries' bank accounts. Over Rs. 52 lakh crore has been transferred through DBT nationwide. ● Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI has empowered millions of individuals and small businesses in rural and remote areas to make fast, secure and low-cost digital payments, significantly advancing financial inclusion. o  UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system. o  UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real-time digital payments. State/UT-wise and District-wise UPI statistics are available at https://www.npci.org.in/product/ecosystem-statistics/upi . ● DigiLocker provides citizens with anytime access to authentic digital documents issued by original issuers. The platform has over 71.66 crore registered users, with more than 936.03 crore documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers. More than 2.18 crore Aadhaar enabled registrations have taken place in the state of Tamil Nadu to avail DigiLocker services. ● Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance (UMANG) provides citizens with a single mobile platform to access government services. The platform offers 2,575 services for individuals, including 17 services integrated by the Government of Tamil Nadu. ● e-Sanjeevani facilitates quick and easy access to doctors and medical specialists directly from your smartphone. The platform has served over 48 crore patients across the country including over 4 crore consultations in the state of Tamil Nadu. ●  To promote linguistic inclusion in digital services, the Government has launched the National Language Translation Mission (NLTM) – BHASHINI , envisaged as a public digital platform for Indian language technologies. The Bhashini platform addresses communication barriers for India’s diverse population. Assisted delivery of services through Common Service Centres (CSCs) Common Services Centres – CSCs are offering government and business services in digital mode enhancing last-mile connectivity in rural areas through Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). Over 800 services are being delivered through CSCs. As of May 2026, 5.01 lakh CSCs are functional across the country (in rural and urban areas), out of which 3.91 lakh CSCs are functional at the Gram Panchayat level (rural). In the State of Tamil Nadu, 18,240 CSCs are currently functional, including 12,112 CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level.  In Dharmapuri district, 498 CSCs are currently functional, including 412 CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level(rural). Building Digital Skills: India’s digital transformation goes beyond mere access; it focuses on empowering people and institutions to use technology effectively, driving inclusive growth, strengthening digital governance, and enabling citizens across the nation. Major initiatives include: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) is one of the world’s largest digital literacy initiatives with over 6.39 Crore persons getting trained nationwide (against the target of 6 Crore). In the state of Tamil Nadu, 14+ lakh candidates were trained under the Scheme, including 64,813 candidates from Dharmapuri district. The scheme was concluded on 31.03.2024. FutureSkills Prime , a collaborative initiative of the Government of India and NASSCOM, provides skilling, reskilling, and upskilling in emerging technologies. So far, over 34 lakh candidates have registered on the portal, with more than 23 lakh enrolled/trained in various courses, including over 5.81 lakh candidates from Tamil Nadu. National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) provides digital literacy and skill development courses, including ACC and CCC, through 56 Centres and a network of over 9,000 partner institutes across the country. 31.92 Lakh+ candidates have been trained by NIELIT during the last three financial years. NIELIT has a strong presence in Tamil Nadu through its Centre at Chennai, and 35+ partner institutes across the State. In the last 03 years, NIELIT has trained/skilled 37500+ candidates in the State of Tamil Nadu. NIELIT Digital University (NDU) Platform: The platform delivers online and blended skill-based industry-aligned courses in emerging technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity etc. So far 2.75 lakh+ candidates have registered under the NIELIT Digital University Platform. In addition to the above, various Government services, including issuance of certificates, pension-related services, and welfare schemes, are delivered through State Government portals and mobile applications. The Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency (TNeGA) has developed the e-Sevai portal, which enables end-to-end online delivery of a wide range of citizen-centric Government services without manual intervention. The digital services can be accessed at https://www.tnesevai.tn.gov.in/ . Budget Allocation and Utilisation: The Digital India Programme is an umbrella programme comprising projects implemented by various Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, each with its own budgetary provisions. MeitY implements eight Central Sector sub-schemes under the Programme, for which no State/UT-wise budget allocation is made. This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada in Lok Sabha on 05.08.2026. **** Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2295635) आगंतुक पटल  : 150 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Electronics & IT Government Expands Digital Infrastructure and Citizen-Centric Services to Bridge the Digital Divide 2.21 Lakh Gram Panchayats Made Service Ready Under BharatNet; 5.01 Lakh Common Service Centres Deliver Digital Services Nationwide प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The status in the state of Tamil Nadu including Dharmapuri District of Tamil Nadu is as under: Towers planned Villages planned Towers on Air Villages covered Tamil Nadu 356 445 257 308 Dharmapuri District 14 22 11 19 ●  As on 30.06.2026, a total of Rs. 1886 crores have been disbursed under various ongoing projects of Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) in Tamil Nadu. Services delivery through Digital Public Infrastructure: Affordable data, assisted digital access points, and interoperable public platforms are enabling citizens to access welfare schemes, make digital payments, pursue online education, and participate in governance. Data costs have plummeted from Rs. 269 per GB in 2014 to roughly Rs. 8-10 per Giga Byte in 2025-26, making India one of the world's cheapest data markets. ● Aadhaar: Aadhaar created a trusted biometric identity platform for secure and instant digital authentication. Over 1.44+ billion Aadhaar numbers have been generated. In Tamil Nadu, over 8.18 crore Aadhaar have been generated. ● Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT): Through Aadhaar-linked DBT, cash benefits from various welfare schemes (318 Schemes of 56 Ministries) are directly transferred into beneficiaries' bank accounts. Over Rs. 52 lakh crore has been transferred through DBT nationwide. ● Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI has empowered millions of individuals and small businesses in rural and remote areas to make fast, secure and low-cost digital payments, significantly advancing financial inclusion. o  UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system. o  UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real-time digital payments. State/UT-wise and District-wise UPI statistics are available at https://www.npci.org.in/product/ecosystem-statistics/upi . ● DigiLocker provides citizens with anytime access to authentic digital documents issued by original issuers. The platform has over 71.66 crore registered users, with more than 936.03 crore documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers. More than 2.18 crore Aadhaar enabled registrations have taken place in the state of Tamil Nadu to avail DigiLocker services. ● Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance (UMANG) provides citizens with a single mobile platform to access government services. The platform offers 2,575 services for individuals, including 17 services integrated by the Government of Tamil Nadu. ● e-Sanjeevani facilitates quick and easy access to doctors and medical specialists directly from your smartphone. The platform has served over 48 crore patients across the country including over 4 crore consultations in the state of Tamil Nadu. ●  To promote linguistic inclusion in digital services, the Government has launched the National Language Translation Mission (NLTM) – BHASHINI , envisaged as a public digital platform for Indian language technologies. The Bhashini platform addresses communication barriers for India’s diverse population. Assisted delivery of services through Common Service Centres (CSCs) Common Services Centres – CSCs are offering government and business services in digital mode enhancing last-mile connectivity in rural areas through Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). Over 800 services are being delivered through CSCs. As of May 2026, 5.01 lakh CSCs are functional across the country (in rural and urban areas), out of which 3.91 lakh CSCs are functional at the Gram Panchayat level (rural). In the State of Tamil Nadu, 18,240 CSCs are currently functional, including 12,112 CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level.  In Dharmapuri district, 498 CSCs are currently functional, including 412 CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level(rural). Building Digital Skills: India’s digital transformation goes beyond mere access; it focuses on empowering people and institutions to use technology effectively, driving inclusive growth, strengthening digital governance, and enabling citizens across the nation. Major initiatives include: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) is one of the world’s largest digital literacy initiatives with over 6.39 Crore persons getting trained nationwide (against the target of 6 Crore). So far, over 34 lakh candidates have registered on the portal, with more than 23 lakh enrolled/trained in various courses, including over 5.81 lakh candidates from Tamil Nadu. NIELIT has a strong presence in Tamil Nadu through its Centre at Chennai, and 35+ partner institutes across the State. In the last 03 years, NIELIT has trained/skilled 37500+ candidates in the State of Tamil Nadu. In addition to the above, various Government services, including issuance of certificates, pension-related services, and welfare schemes, are delivered through State Government portals and mobile applications. The Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency (TNeGA) has developed the e-Sevai portal, which enables end-to-end online delivery of a wide range of citizen-centric Government services without manual intervention. The digital services can be accessed at https://www.tnesevai.tn.gov.in/ . Budget Allocation and Utilisation: The Digital India Programme is an umbrella programme comprising projects implemented by various Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, each with its own budgetary provisions. MeitY implements eight Central Sector sub-schemes under the Programme, for which no State/UT-wise budget allocation is made.
